---
title: "Run JAXCMR in VS Code"
description: "Set up Python and a JAXCMR notebook on an Apple Silicon Mac."
---

By the end of this page, you will have a folder for your work, a Python
environment with JAXCMR installed, and a notebook that can run Python code.
You do not need previous Python experience or a research dataset.

For browser-based execution, follow the [Colab instructions](templates.qmd#run-in-colab)
instead. That route installs the library inside a hosted notebook.

These instructions are for an **Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer)** with an
internet connection. You can find your Mac's chip under **Apple menu → About
This Mac**. Allow time for the initial downloads.

::: {.callout-note}
## Release status

This page targets **JAXCMR 0.2.0**, which is not yet available on
[PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/jaxcmr/). The installation command below needs
that release. Publication and confirmation of these steps in a fresh environment
are still required before this local setup is ready to use.
:::

## 1. Install the editor

Download [Visual Studio Code for Mac](https://code.visualstudio.com/download),
open the download, drag the app into **Applications**, and launch it.

Open **Extensions** from the left sidebar, or press **Shift–Command–X**.
Install **Python** and **Jupyter**, both published by Microsoft. These extensions
let VS Code edit and run Python notebooks.

## 2. Create a working folder

In Finder, open **Documents** and create a folder named **jaxcmr-workshop**.
In VS Code, choose **File → Open Folder…** and open that folder. If VS Code asks
whether you trust this folder, confirm for the folder you just created.

Choose **Terminal → New Terminal**. The terminal is the panel where you enter
installation commands. Later, you will enter Python code into a notebook cell;
the terminal and the notebook are separate places to enter code.

## 3. Install Python and packages

Run these commands in the terminal **one at a time**. Press Return after each
command and wait until the prompt reappears before continuing:

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | env UV_UNMANAGED_INSTALL="$PWD/.tools" sh
.tools/uv venv --python 3.12 --managed-python --seed .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install "jaxcmr==0.2.0" "ipykernel>=6.29.5"
```

The first command downloads **uv**, which can install Python for you. The second
creates a **Python 3.12 environment** in this folder's `.venv` directory. An
environment keeps the Python and packages for this work together. The third
installs JAXCMR and the package that runs Python inside a notebook.

The commands name this environment directly, so you do not need an activation
command or an existing Python installation. The first downloads can take
several minutes. See uv's [installer options](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/installer/)
and [Python installation guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/install-python/)
for details.

## 4. Create a notebook and select its environment

Press **Shift–Command–P** to open VS Code's Command Palette. Choose
**Create: New Jupyter Notebook**. Save the new notebook as **setup-check.ipynb**
inside your `jaxcmr-workshop` folder.

Click **Select Kernel** at the upper right of the notebook. If a kernel is
already selected, click its name and choose **Select Another Kernel…**. Choose
**Python Environments…**, then the Python 3.12 environment whose location ends
in `jaxcmr-workshop/.venv/bin/python`.

A *kernel* is the Python process that runs the notebook's cells. Selecting this
kernel tells the notebook to use the environment where you installed JAXCMR.
See the [VS Code notebook guide](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/jupyter-notebooks)
and [kernel selection instructions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/datascience/jupyter-kernel-management).

## 5. Run the setup cell

Paste this code into the notebook's first code cell, then click the triangle
beside the cell to run it:

```python
import sys
import jax.numpy as jnp
import jaxcmr

print("Python:", sys.version.split()[0])
print("Environment:", sys.executable)
print("JAXCMR:", jaxcmr.__version__)
print("JAX calculation:", int(jnp.arange(4).sum()))
```

You should see four lines like these:

```text
Python: 3.12.…
Environment: /Users/your-name/Documents/jaxcmr-workshop/.venv/bin/python
JAXCMR: 0.2.0
JAX calculation: 6
```

Your Python patch version and username will differ. The environment path should
point inside your working folder's `.venv`, the JAXCMR version should be
**0.2.0**, and the calculation should give **6**. The calculation adds the
numbers 0, 1, 2 and 3 using JAX.

This establishes that your notebook can use the installed packages. No model
or dataset is needed for this step.

## 6. Save and return later

Save the notebook with **Command–S**. When you return, open the same folder and
notebook in VS Code and select the same `.venv` kernel.

Use **Restart Kernel**, then **Run All**, to run the notebook in a fresh Python
session. You should see the same four results. Saved output records an earlier
run; restarting the kernel clears its working memory, so cells need to run
again before later cells can use their results.

## If a step fails

| What you see | What to do |
|---|---|
| `.tools/uv` or `.venv/bin/python` cannot be found | Check that VS Code has your `jaxcmr-workshop` folder open. Open a new terminal there and complete step 3 in order. |
| `.venv` is missing from the kernel list | Confirm step 3 finished successfully. Close and reopen the folder, then select the notebook kernel again. |
| VS Code asks to install `ipykernel` | Re-run the final command in step 3, then select this folder's `.venv` kernel. |
| `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jaxcmr'` | Check the selected kernel's path. Select this folder's `.venv` and, if necessary, re-run the final installation command. |
| The printed JAXCMR version is not `0.2.0` | Check the environment path and reselect the correct kernel. Re-run the pinned installation command after confirming that the release is available. |
| pip cannot find `jaxcmr==0.2.0` | Check the release-status note above. This setup cannot be completed until that version is available; do not substitute an older version. |

If an error remains, keep its text and any setup-cell output so the person
helping you can identify the environment and the failing step.

## Continue with fitting

Once the setup cell runs successfully, start with **[Fitting a model](templates/fitting_scipyde.ipynb)**.
It brings together parameter estimation, simulation and behavioral analyses,
ending with saved results and figures comparing model predictions with observations.

Follow [From a template to a run](templates.qmd#from-a-template-to-a-run) to place
the notebook and its inputs in your working folder and use the environment you
have just created. The notebook's saved example shows the complete procedure;
its **parameters** cell configures the run you execute.
